name: errands-op
description: An intelligent, offline-first errand optimizer bridging Home Assistant with advanced VRPTW algorithms and learned aisle-sorting logic.
readme:
errands-op

Flutter errand optimizer with Home Assistant sync and VRP solver

---

errands-op is an offline-first, algorithmic errand routing engine. It bridges Home Assistant to-do lists, solves multi-stop Vehicle Routing Problems with Time Windows (VRPTW), prevents false GPS triggers with dual-ring hysteresis geofencing, and learns in-store aisle walk-orders through Feedback Arc Set cycle elimination and topological sorting.

--- ## ⚡ Why errands-op? Most errand organizers either force-sort your personal list into an unfamiliar sequence or ignore the practical realities of shopping—such as frozen groceries melting while you visit the hardware store, or GPS bouncing while driving by a plaza.

--- ## 🏗️ System Architecture `errands-op` executes a closed-loop four-stage mathematical pipeline:

### 1. Home Assistant Sync & Hybrid Logical Clocks - Bi-directional sync with any Home Assistant to-do entity over `/api/websocket` (`todo/item/subscribe` snapshots + `todo.add_item` / `update_item` / `remove_item`), matched by HA's item `uid`. Remote adds, renames, completions and deletions flow in; items from voice assistants get a category and perishable flag guessed from their text. - Offline-first mutation queue ordered by **Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC)**, compacted per item/field, with **Last-Write-Wins (LWW)**: unsent local edits win over incoming snapshots. Order, pins, categories and perishable flags stay local. - Exponential backoff with random jitter and a 30 s heartbeat; a rejected token stops retrying and is shown in Settings. ### 2. Hybrid VRPTW Multi-Stop Sequence Solver - **Exact label-setting DP**: Store choice and visit order are solved *jointly* by a dynamic program over (tasks covered, last store) with Pareto pruning on (time, cost), run on a background isolate. Lists with more than 12 distinct tasks fall back to a greedy cost-per-task heuristic. - **Disjunctive Candidate Matching**: Each item can be served by any store stocking its category; one stop can serve several categories. Strongly learned favourite stores filter out the rest, weaker preferences act as a soft cost. - **Time Windows**: Arrives early → waits for opening ($\beta$ wait penalty); service must finish before closing. Overnight hours (e.g. 18:00–02:00) are supported. - **Thermal Decay Penalty**: $\gamma = 0.5$ per perishable item per second carried until you're home, so cold items are bought late — even if it means buying them at a different store than the rest. - **Human Hard Sequence Locks**: A pinned (📌) item is never served after anything listed below it ($t_A + s_A + C_{AB} \le t_B$). - **Constraint Relaxation Cascade**: If no route meets every closing time (e.g. because of pins), windows become soft penalties, the pinned order is kept, and each late stop gets an explicit warning. - **Distance Matrix**: Optional OSRM-compatible routing server with geohash-6 caching (7-day TTL); otherwise Haversine × road tortuosity ($\tau = 1.28$) at ~40 km/h. The route includes the trip home. ### 3. Dual-Ring Hysteresis Geofencing State Machine - **2D Kalman GPS Filter**: Discards noisy fixes with horizontal accuracy $\sigma > 30\text{m}$. - **Inner Arrival Ring** (each store's own radius, 40 m by default): requires a continuous $120\text{s}$ dwell before transitioning to `INSIDE_STORE` mode. - **Outer Exit Ring** (2 × the arrival radius): an exit grace buffer of $180\text{s}$ prevents premature session termination when walking through store dead zones. Distances are always measured to the store you are in, so a neighbouring shop can't hold or end your visit. - Live GPS via `geolocator` (Android/iOS/macOS); visits left open by an app restart are resumed or closed. ### 4. Learned In-Store Layout Walk-Order (DAG) - Observes real timestamped item check-offs inside stores ($\tau_1 < \tau_2 < \dots < \tau_m$). - Computes exponential decay precedence weights: $w(\Delta \tau) = \exp(-(\tau_B - \tau_A)/\sigma)$ and **accumulates** them as evidence per store (both directions are kept). - **Net DAG + Feedback Arc Set (FAS)**: Opposite directions cancel out; remaining cycles are broken by cutting the edge with the least evidence. - **Kahn's Topological Sort**: Produces the empirical walk order; categories the store hasn't learned yet keep your own list order. --- ## 📱 Application Screens | Screen | Responsibility | | :--- | :--- | | **Main Errand List** | Reorderable list preserving manual sequence (also while filtered), tap-to-edit, non-destructive overlay badges (`Stop #1`, `Stop #2`), filter chips, and "I'm Going Out" solver CTA. | | **Route Itinerary** | Step-by-step timeline with arrival estimates, closing hour conflict alerts, and travel distances. | | **Radar Map** | Interactive radar canvas rendering GPS fix, store nodes, route polylines, and dual geofence rings ($40\text{m} / 80\text{m}$). | | **In-Store Shopping Mode** | Auto-triggered upon geofence dwell. Groups items by store aisle and sorts them via the learned DAG toposort. | | **Stores & DAG** | Add, edit and delete stores (location, hours, time spent, categories, arrival radius) and inspect each store's learned walk graph. | | **Settings & Simulator** | Home Assistant connection, live GPS, home location, optional routing server, and a sandbox to simulate GPS fixes, store visits and remote HA items. | --- ## 🚀 Quick Start ### Prerequisites - [Flutter SDK](https://flutter.dev) 3.47+ (Dart 3.13+) - Android: Android SDK (API 36) — `flutter doctor` lists anything missing - Linux desktop: `sudo apt install clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config libgtk-3-dev libsqlite3-dev` - The web target is not supported (local data lives in SQLite). ### Setup & Run ```bash git clone https://github.com/seeramsujay/errands-op.git cd errands-op flutter pub get flutter test # 64 tests flutter run # connected phone or desktop flutter build apk --release ``` ### First-time setup in the app 1. **Stores & DAG → Add Store** for the shops and offices you use (the five Bangalore stores are sample data). 2. **Settings → Location**: set your home (route start/end) and turn on **Live GPS**. 3. **Settings → Home Assistant** (optional): paste your HA URL (e.g. `http://homeassistant.local:8123`), a long-lived access token (HA → Profile → Security) and the to-do entity (default `todo.shopping_list`). Items you added before connecting are pushed on first connect. 4. Optional: an OSRM server URL for real road travel times. --- ## 🧪 Test Suite ```bash flutter test # 00:06 +64: All tests passed! # - vrp_solver_test joint store choice, thermal deferral, waiting for opening, closing-time ordering, # pins & relaxation cascade, overnight hours, heuristic fallback, <1.5 s for 12 tasks # - layout_learning_test Kahn's sort, FAS, evidence accumulation, end-to-end visit learning # - geofence_engine_test Kalman gating, dwell/grace timing, neighbouring stores, per-store radius, restart recovery # - sync_engine_test real WebSocket against a fake Home Assistant: auth, snapshots, uid adoption, # remote deletes, offline queue compaction, bad token, reconnect # - app_state_test filtered reorder, editing, overlays, persisted routes, store CRUD, reset # - database_test v1 → v2 migration, seeding, retry parking, category classifier # - widget_test / app_smoke_test item tile, full app boot + every tab at phone width ``` --- ## 📄 License Distributed under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for more details.

name: event-manager
description: GenAI-powered planning assistant for weddings and events, featuring deterministic logic, interactive budget tools, and WCAG-compliant accessibility.
readme:
event-manager

GenAI-powered planning assistant for weddings, birthdays and community events: budgets, timelines, vendor checklists and personalized ideas.

--- # Plan Together: GenAI Event Planning Assistant [![CI](https://github.com/seeramsujay/event-manager/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seeramsujay/event-manager/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-622%20passing-brightgreen) ![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-100%25%20lines-brightgreen) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A522.9-blue) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) [![Live Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live%20demo-Vercel-black?logo=vercel)](https://event-manager-alpha-hazel.vercel.app) An intelligent, accessible, zero-dependency assistant that helps people organize **weddings, birthdays, and community events**. You describe your event (date, guest count, budget, location, setting, style, priorities, and special considerations) and it synthesizes a production-grade plan grounded in deterministic arithmetic and fast GenAI creativity: | Part of the plan | What you get | |---|---| | 🌟 **Landing page & smooth scroll** | Clean hero introduction with key value propositions and a keyboard/reduced-motion-aware smooth-scroll CTA to the planner form | | 📍 **Smart location & local nuance** | Auto-prompts for geolocation on load, detects city via privacy-preserving reverse geocoding, and adapts plan to municipal curfews (10 PM sound rules), permits, and Google Maps vendor searches | | 📊 **Interactive budget breakdown** | Adaptive SVG donut chart with synchronized hover inspection: donut center updates dynamically to amount & share while non-hovered categories smoothly dim | | 💡 **Explain this plan** | Instant architectural breakdown explaining budget tier classifications, schedule compression factors, venue scale strategy, and core risk defenses | | 🗓️ **Timeline & backward scheduling** | Milestones scheduled backwards from your event date with automatic proportional compression for short lead times | | ✅ **Vendor checklist & local search** | Categorized vendors with priority badges, deadlines, local tips, and direct 1-click Google Maps discovery links | | 🤖 **AI Agent Copilot & Parser** | Tailored discovery questions (food tastes, vibe, accessibility), one-click structured prompt export for ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini, and an intelligent answer parser that injects an **Agent Strategy Brief** into your plan | | ⚠️ **Context-aware insights** | Proactive defenses for rushed schedules, tight budgets, municipal ordinances, vendor travel radii, weather contingencies, and accessibility | | ✨ **Personalized ideas via Gemini 2.5** | Local seasonal menus, signature cocktail/mocktail tasting stations, and decor themes powered by **Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite** (with instant catalog fallback) | | ♿ **Accessibility toolbar** | Expandable WCAG 2.2 AAA toolbar: font scaling (Large 118%), High Contrast mode, and forced reduced motion with zero-flash persistence | | 📥 **Universal exports** | 1-click **Download Markdown** (`.md` with tables & checklists), **Download JSON** (full structured plan), and clean Print styling | --- ## Contents 1. [Live Demo](#live-demo) 2. [Chosen vertical](#chosen-vertical) 3. [Approach and architecture](#approach-and-architecture) 4. [Key features in action](#key-features-in-action) 5. [Getting started](#getting-started) 6. [Configuration](#configuration) 7. [Engineering quality: security, testing, accessibility](#engineering-quality) 8. [License](#license) --- ## Live Demo 🚀 **Production Deployment:** [https://event-manager-alpha-hazel.vercel.app](https://event-manager-alpha-hazel.vercel.app) Try generating plans across different constraints: - **Weddings:** 150 guests, \$35,000 budget, outdoor setting, photography priority. - **Birthdays:** 10th birthday for kids, alcohol-free, low-waste, hybrid setting. - **Community Festivals:** 500 attendees, municipal permits, safety/EMS thresholds. --- ## Chosen vertical **Event Planning Assistant.** The target persona is a host or community organizer: a couple planning their wedding, a parent throwing a birthday party, or a neighborhood volunteer organizing a cultural festival. They are not professional event producers; they need realistic, enforceable guidance that respects their budget, timeline, and local regulations. Three event verticals are deeply modeled: 1. **Weddings:** Long lead times (ideal 52 weeks), day-of coordination thresholds ($\ge 150$ guests), ceremony/reception transitions, officiants, florists, and photography. 2. **Birthdays:** Age-adaptive logic (kids $\le 12$ get kid-friendly supervision, nut-free snacks, and entertainer booking; adults get bartending and milestone tribute tasks for 21, 30, 40, etc.). 3. **Community Events:** Municipal authorities & permits ($\ge 300$ attendees), first aid & emergency services ($\ge 200$), crowd flow, outdoor canopy rentals, and waste/recycling stations. --- ## Approach and architecture The application is architected around a strict principle: **Deterministic rules engine for critical math and logistics, GenAI for creativity and thematic nuance.** ```mermaid flowchart LR B[Browser Client
public/ · Vanilla JS] -- POST /api/plan --> A[HTTP Server
Node.js / Vercel Edge] B -. GET /api/geocode .-> A A --> V[validation.js
Strict Zod Schema + Calendar Rules] V --> P[planner/index.js
buildPlan — Pure & Deterministic] P --> BU[budget.js
Largest-Remainder Split] P --> T[timeline.js
Backward Scheduling] P --> VE[vendors.js
Priorities & Maps Search] P --> I[insights.js
Municipal & Risk Defense] P --> Q[questions.js
Discovery Copilot] P --> AI[ai/ideas.js
Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite] AI -- Structured JSON --> G[(Gemini API)] AI -. on failure / offline .-> CU[Curated Theme Catalog] AI --> A A -- Complete Plan JSON --> B ``` ### Deterministic Engine (`src/planner/`) - **Budget Allocator:** Uses the **largest-remainder method** (Hamilton-Hare) so allocated cents always sum to $100\%$ of the budget without rounding drift. Category weights scale dynamically with user priorities ($\times 1.25$) and setting requirements. - **Timeline Engine:** Calculates ideal lead dates backwards from the event date. If time is short, it executes proportional compression without inverted dates or past deadlines, automatically flagging overdue vendors as **Book now**. - **Context Insights:** Automatically warns of municipal sound curfews (e.g. 10 PM residential noise limits), vendor travel radius charges, weather backup tents (+3% reserve), and required permits. - **Discovery Questions:** Assembles targeted questions regarding guest food preferences, vibe/lighting desires, and accessibility needs. ### GenAI Creativity Layer (`src/ai/`) - **Model:** Google **Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite** (`gemini-2.5-flash-lite`), providing sub-second structured JSON responses. - **Grounding:** Injects the engine's computed budget tier, location, guest profile, setting, and key logistical risks into the prompt. - **Resilience:** If no API key is supplied, or during rate limits or network failures, the planner automatically falls back to an extensive curated idea catalog with zero user disruption. --- ## Key features in action ### 1. Interactive Budget Donut & Synchronized Row Highlighting - Visualizes spending distribution with an SVG donut chart. - **Default center display:** Formatted total event budget. - **Hover interaction:** Hovering any slice or table row highlights that category, displays its exact dollar amount, category title, and percentage in the donut center, while dimming all other rows and slices to 30% opacity. - **Side share percentage:** Percentage numbers are cleanly positioned outside progress bars in a dedicated tabular column to prevent text clipping. ### 2. External AI Agent Copilot & Import Parser - **📋 Copy Agent Prompt:** Generates an exhaustive prompt embedded with your event's specific budget tier, guest count, setting, and discovery questions. - **📥 Import Agent Answers:** Paste the response from ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini into the import drawer. The parser automatically structures the recommendations into an **Agent Strategy Brief** card embedded into the live plan and included in Markdown/JSON exports. ### 3. Native Export Capabilities - **Download Markdown (`.md`):** Clean GitHub-flavored Markdown with formatted tables, task checklists (`- [ ]`), vendor booking dates, and AI ideas. - **Download JSON:** Full structured data payload for integration into spreadsheets or external tools. - **Print Optimization:** Specialized `@media print` stylesheet with dedicated header, footer, zero bar clipping, and page-break protection. ### 4. Privacy-Preserving Geolocation & Maps Discovery - Automatically prompts for browser location on load if empty. - Coordinates are rounded to 3 decimal places (~110m privacy buffer) before reverse geocoding through an in-memory cached proxy. - Vendor checklist provides instant **Google Maps search links** configured for the selected vendor type and city. --- ## Getting started Requires **Node.js 22.9+** and **pnpm**. ```bash git clone https://github.com/seeramsujay/event-manager.git cd event-manager pnpm install cp .env.example .env # optional: add GEMINI_API_KEY for live AI ideas pnpm start # → http://127.0.0.1:3000 ``` Without an API key, the application operates fully in offline/curated mode. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `pnpm start` | Runs the server in production mode | | `pnpm run dev` | Runs with auto-restart on file modifications | | `pnpm test` | Runs the entire 622-test test suite | | `pnpm run test:coverage` | Enforces 100% line coverage and high branch coverage | | `pnpm run lint` | Runs ESLint across the codebase | | `pnpm run check` | Runs lint + 100% coverage gate (identical to CI) | --- ## Configuration All configuration is handled via environment variables validated at boot: | Variable | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | (optional) | Google Gemini API key for real-time generative ideas | | `GEMINI_MODEL` | `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | Gemini model name | | `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP listening port | | `HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Network interface (`0.0.0.0` in containers) | | `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `20` | Bounded sliding-window rate limit per client IP | | `TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | Set to `true` behind reverse proxies (Vercel, Cloudflare, Nginx) | --- ## Engineering quality ### 🧪 622 Automated Tests (100% Line Coverage) - **Property-based tests:** Over 2,000 randomized synthetic plans verified against invariant laws: zero budget drift, monotonic chronological timelines, and safe prompt bounds. - **Browser DOM integration tests (jsdom):** Full UI audit covering accessibility attributes, focus traps, error summaries, interactive chart hover states, checklist persistence across storage, and export downloads. - **Security & HTTP audit:** Verified against XSS injections, path traversal allowlists, HTTP header compliance (`Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'`), rate limiting, and request body streaming caps. ### ♿ Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA / AAA Compliant) - **Accessibility Options Panel:** Zero-flash persistence for **Large Font Scaling (118%)**, **WCAG AAA High Contrast**, and **Forced Reduced Motion**. - **Keyboard Navigation:** 100% operable with clear focus rings, skip-to-content links, and scoped ARIA live announcements. - **Color Contrast:** Exceeds 4.5:1 in standard themes and 7:1 in High Contrast mode. --- ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

name: homework-bud
description: Modernized Graves RNN for personalized handwriting synthesis, featuring computer vision line detection and realistic ink rendering for PDF compilation.
readme:
Homework-Bud

Personalized Handwriting Synthesis with Graves RNNs on Real Ruled Notebook Sheets

--- ## 🌟 Overview **Homework-Bud** adapts and extends Alex Graves' seminal handwriting synthesis recurrent neural network ([*Generating Sequences with Recurrent Neural Networks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0850)) into a production-ready assignment generator: 1. **Modernized RNN Engine**: Fully modernized for **TensorFlow 2.x** with all legacy `tf.contrib` dependencies eliminated, supporting both CPU and GPU execution. 2. **Ruled Sheet Detection (`ruled_sheet_detector.py`)**: Uses computer vision (Hough line transforms, projection profiles, and contour analysis) to detect baseline positions, line heights, and margin boundaries directly from photos of notebook pages (e.g., [`Blank_Page.jpeg`](Blank_Page.jpeg)). 3. **Realistic Ink Simulation (`scan_renderer.py`)**: Simulates realistic ballpoint and gel pen strokes (including authentic Royal Blue ink pigments, micro-jitter, velocity-dependent stroke thickness, and realistic alpha-blending onto paper textures). 4. **Personal Style Extraction & Fine-Tuning (`line_segmenter.py`, `finetune_user.py`)**: Slices photographs of user handwriting into individual lines, aligns them with verified ground-truth transcriptions ([`lines_transcription.csv`](lines_transcription.csv)), extracts vector strokes, and fine-tunes the RNN model to mimic personal handwriting. 5. **Multi-Page Essay Compilation (`homework_engine.py`)**: Word-wraps long essays across page boundaries, synthesizes strokes line-by-line, and compiles high-resolution multi-page PDF assignments. 6. **Turnkey Kaggle Integration (`kaggle/`)**: Pre-configured kernels and automated builders for training and multi-page generation on Kaggle GPUs. --- ## 📁 Repository Structure ``` homework-bud/ ├── Blank_Page.jpeg # Default high-res photo of blank ruled notebook paper ├── lines_transcription.csv # Verified line transcriptions for user handwriting training ├── pyproject.toml # Project metadata and dependencies ├── requirements.txt # Pip requirements │ ├── checkpoints/ # Pretrained Graves RNN weights (model-17900) ├── styles/ # Pretrained style vectors (styles 0-12 and user style) ├── data/ # Data utilities and IAM character blacklists ├── img/ # Banner and documentation assets │ ├── Core Handwriting Synthesis (Graves RNN TF 2.x): │ ├── demo.py # High-level Hand synthesis interface │ ├── drawing.py # Stroke tokenization, encoding & SVG rendering │ ├── rnn.py # Graves RNN architecture with soft window attention & GMM loss │ ├── rnn_cell.py # Custom LSTM & Mixture Density Network cells │ ├── rnn_ops.py # GMM ops and parameter extraction │ ├── tf_base_model.py # TensorFlow model wrapper and training loop │ ├── tf_utils.py # Session and checkpoint utilities │ ├── data_frame.py # Batch data feeder │ └── lyrics.py # Original demo lyrics │ ├── Homework-Bud Pipeline: │ ├── homework_engine.py # Central orchestrator: pagination, synthesis, and PDF compilation │ ├── ruled_sheet_detector.py # CV detector for page lines, line heights, and margins │ ├── scan_renderer.py # Ink texture simulation, stroke jitter, paper blending │ ├── line_segmenter.py # Slices user handwriting photos into line crops │ ├── paper_stroke_extractor.py # Vector stroke skeletonizer from image crops │ ├── build_dataset_verified.py # Generates stroke .npy dataset from verified transcriptions │ ├── build_dataset_ocr.py # TrOCR neural OCR dataset builder │ ├── finetune_user.py # Fine-tunes pretrained model on user handwriting │ └── extract_style.py # Extracts style conditioning vectors from user samples │ └── kaggle/ # Kaggle GPU workflows & pipelines ├── README.md # Kaggle workflow documentation ├── builders/ # Generators for Kaggle Jupyter notebooks │ ├── build_kaggle_notebook.py │ ├── build_generator_notebook.py │ ├── build_original_style_notebook.py │ └── build_all.py # Regenerates all Kaggle notebooks ├── kernels/ # Self-contained Kaggle kernels │ ├── finetune/ # Model fine-tuning notebook & metadata │ ├── essay_generator/ # 1,000+ word essay generator notebook & metadata │ └── style6_generator/ # Style 6 maximum-legibility notebook & metadata └── dataset/ # Kaggle dataset management ├── dataset-metadata.json # Dataset metadata for sujaykid/homework-bud-data └── stage_dataset.py # Script to stage dataset bundle for upload ``` --- ## 🚀 Quickstart ### 1. Installation Create a virtual environment and install the required dependencies: ```bash # Using uv (recommended) uv venv source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -r requirements.txt # Or using standard pip python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ### 2. Generating Handwritten Assignments Locally ```python from homework_engine import HomeworkEngine # Initialize the homework engine (loads base model-17900 checkpoint) engine = HomeworkEngine( checkpoint_dir="checkpoints", styles_dir="styles" ) essay_text = """ The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Modern Society Artificial intelligence has rapidly transitioned from a theoretical concept into an integral force shaping every facet of our everyday lives. From autonomous transportation to advanced medical diagnostics, machine learning models are augmenting human capabilities at an unprecedented rate. As we look toward the future, the responsible development of ethical AI systems will be critical in maximizing their benefits while preserving transparency and fairness. """ # Generate ruled homework pages in Royal Blue ink output_pages, pdf_path = engine.generate_homework( text=essay_text, blank_sheet_paths=["Blank_Page.jpeg"], output_dir="output", style_id=6, # Use Style 6 for maximum legibility (or None for user style) bias=1.0, # Higher bias (0.9 - 1.0) produces neat, uniform handwriting ink_color="royal_blue" ) print(f"Generated PDF: {pdf_path}") ``` --- ## ⚡ Kaggle Pipelines When generating long essays or training on large handwriting datasets, Homework-Bud provides dedicated GPU workflows in [`kaggle/`](kaggle/): | Kernel | Description | Path | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Stage 2 Fine-Tuning** | Fine-tunes the base RNN on personal user handwriting (`lines_transcription.csv`) | `kaggle/kernels/finetune/` | | **Essay Generator** | Generates 1,000+ word multi-page assignments using custom conditioned style | `kaggle/kernels/essay_generator/` | | **Style 6 Generator** | Generates multi-page assignments using pretrained Style 6 with maximum legibility | `kaggle/kernels/style6_generator/` | ### Regenerate Notebooks If you modify builder logic, regenerate all 3 Kaggle notebooks with: ```bash python kaggle/builders/build_all.py ``` ### Push Kernels to Kaggle ```bash kaggle kernels push -p kaggle/kernels/finetune kaggle kernels push -p kaggle/kernels/essay_generator kaggle kernels push -p kaggle/kernels/style6_generator ``` ### Stage & Upload Dataset Bundle To upload or update the dataset `sujaykid/homework-bud-data` without committing duplicate files to Git: ```bash python kaggle/dataset/stage_dataset.py kaggle datasets version -p kaggle/dataset/bundle -m "Update dataset" --dir-mode zip ``` --- ## 🔬 How It Works ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Input Text / Essay"] --> B["HomeworkEngine (Pagination & Word-Wrap)"] C["Blank_Page.jpeg"] --> D["RuledSheetDetector (Hough Lines & Margins)"] D --> B B --> E["Alex Graves RNN Synthesis (TF 2.x)"] F["Styles / User Stroke Conditioning"] --> E E --> G["Raw Coordinates & Pen Lifts"] G --> H["ScanRenderer (Ink Bleed, Jitter & Blue Pigment)"] C --> H H --> I["Composite Handwritten Ruled Pages"] I --> J["Multi-Page Submission PDF"] ``` 1. **Ruled Sheet Analysis**: [`ruled_sheet_detector.py`](ruled_sheet_detector.py) identifies horizontal line coordinates, calculating median line height and margin offsets so text aligns naturally between ruled lines. 2. **Sequential Character Attention**: The recurrent network predicts handwriting strokes sequentially using Gaussian Mixture Models conditioned on character sequences and style vectors. 3. **Scan Rendering**: [`scan_renderer.py`](scan_renderer.py) renders the coordinate sequence with cubic splines, introducing micro-variations in line thickness, realistic stroke overlaps, and color jitter to authentically replicate real ballpoint or gel ink. 4. **Compilation**: Individual pages are saved as high-resolution PNGs and assembled into a multi-page PDF using ReportLab. --- ## 📜 License & Acknowledgements - Core handwriting synthesis architecture based on Alex Graves' paper [*Generating Sequences with Recurrent Neural Networks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0850) and the open-source implementation by [Sean Vasquez](https://github.com/sjvasquez/handwriting-synthesis). - Homework-Bud enhancements, ruled paper detection, ink rendering, dataset pipelines, and Kaggle integration created by [Sujay S](https://github.com/seeramsujay).

name: hrmagent
description: An autonomous coding agent framework optimized for sub-6GB VRAM, leveraging hierarchical latent reasoning to solve complex software engineering tasks.
readme:
hrmagent

**HRM-4M** is an autonomous coding agent framework engineered for resource-constrained hardware (consumer laptop GPUs with $\le 6$ GB VRAM). It overcomes the historical "intelligence ceiling" of sub-2B parameter models on complex multi-file software engineering and competitive programming by synthes

--- # HRM-4M: Hierarchical Reasoning Model Autonomous Coding Agent [![CI Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/CI-Passing-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/seeramsujay/hrmagent/actions) [![TerminalBench](https://img.shields.io/badge/TerminalBench-100%25%20(5%2F5)-success.svg)](reports/benchmark_report.md) [![CodeChef Benchmark](https://img.shields.io/badge/CodeChef%20Benchmark-100%25%20AC-blue.svg)](reports/benchmark_report.md) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.10%20%7C%203.11%20%7C%203.12-blue.svg)](pyproject.toml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE) **HRM-4M** is an autonomous coding agent framework engineered for resource-constrained hardware (consumer laptop GPUs with $\le 6$ GB VRAM). It overcomes the historical "intelligence ceiling" of sub-2B parameter models on complex multi-file software engineering and competitive programming by synthesizing **continuous latent-space recurrent reasoning** with a **four-tier collaborative division of labor**. --- ## Key Highlights - **Model 1 (HRM Latent Reasoner)**: Dual-timescale continuous recurrence engine ($H \times L$) based on Sapient HRM. Discovers mathematical, algorithmic, and state-space invariants entirely in latent space without generating verbose text Chain-of-Thought (CoT) tokens. - **Model 2 (Supervisor Planner)**: System 2 macro-planner that enforces **Context Slicing ($< 8,000$ tokens)**, complexity bounds, numbered edit checklists, and standard I/O driver framing. - **Model 3 (Code-Action Worker)**: System 1 fast worker operating via executable Python code-actions (`smolagents` style) with atomic tools and literal `SEARCH / REPLACE` diff blocks across Kotlin, TypeScript, and Python. - **Model 4 (Jev Verifier & Critic)**: Closed-loop sandboxed execution measuring `os.wait4` CPU time and peak RSS memory telemetry, diagnosing asymptotic bottlenecks, and driving automated self-repair. - **100% TerminalBench Pass Rate**: 5/5 tasks passed in **287.1 ms** total wall-clock time across log diagnostics, code patching, C++20 64-bit compilation, recursive shell refactoring, and unit test repair. - **100% CodeChef Benchmark Pass Rate**: Solved 10/10 challenges across Game Theory, Dynamic Programming, Greedy Interval Scheduling, Median Selection, Binary Search, and Sieve Number Theory (vs 10.0% for baseline sub-1B). - **Sub-2.1 GB Active VRAM**: Hosted resident on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU at **78–103 tokens/sec** throughput. - **Zero Cloud API Dependencies**: Runs 100% locally with an OpenAI-compatible REST server. --- ## Architecture Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Tier1["Tier 1: Latent Reasoning (HRM-1B / 27M)"] Spec[Problem Statement & Constraints] --> LatentHRM["HRM Recurrent Engine\nDual-Timescale Recurrence (H x L)\nContinuous State Injection (z_L + z_H)"] LatentHRM --> Invariant["Converged Latent Invariant\n(0 Text CoT Tokens Wasted)"] end subgraph Tier2["Tier 2: System 2 Supervisor (Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B)"] Invariant --> Sup["Supervisor Planner"] Sup --> Slices["Context Slices < 8000 Tok\nNumbered Edit Checklist\nComplexity Bounds"] end subgraph Tier3["Tier 3: Code-Action Worker (Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B / Maincoder-1B)"] Slices --> Worker["Code-Action Worker\n(smolagents paradigm)"] Worker --> Actions["Atomic Tools: read, write, run\nSEARCH / REPLACE Diff Blocks"] end subgraph Tier4["Tier 4: Jev Verifier & Oracle (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B + Sandbox)"] Actions --> Sandbox["SandboxRunner\nos.wait4 Telemetry (CPU & MaxRSS)"] Sandbox -->|Pass AC| Complete["Verified Production Solution"] Sandbox -->|Fail / Bottleneck| Critic["Jev Critic Analysis"] Critic -->|Targeted Patch Directive| Worker Critic -->|Escalate Paradigm| Sup end ``` --- ## Directory Structure ```text hrmagent/ ├── pyproject.toml # Python dependencies & build configuration (PEP 621) ├── README.md # Primary overview and quickstart guide ├── configs/ │ ├── models.yaml # Model topologies, GGUF paths, and KV cache configs │ └── training.yaml # NVIDIA GPU LoRA hyperparameters & supervisor-worker settings ├── data/ │ ├── codechef_raw.json # 15 rich CodeChef competitive programming challenges │ └── curated/ # Curated training JSONLs (10k+ stars code, CP blueprints, DPO pairs) ├── docs/ │ ├── ARCHITECTURE.md # In-depth architectural & mathematical specification │ ├── API_REFERENCE.md # Complete CLI & REST API documentation │ ├── BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md # TerminalBench & CodeChef evaluation instructions │ └── HRM_FOUR_MODEL_PAPER.md # Academic research paper preprint draft ├── grammars/ │ ├── planner.gbnf # GBNF grammar for System 2 JSON blueprints │ ├── critic.gbnf # GBNF grammar for Jev Critic verdicts │ └── unified_diff.gbnf # GBNF grammar for strict unified diff patches ├── outputs/ │ ├── hrm_4m_vs_baseline_comparison.json # 4M vs Baseline head-to-head benchmark results │ ├── terminal_bench_report.json # TerminalBench execution summary │ └── checkpoints_hrm_latent/ # Trained HRM latent reasoner weights (.pt) ├── reports/ │ └── benchmark_report.md # Hardware profiling, telemetry, and ablation reports ├── scripts/ │ └── run_nvidia_eval.py # NVIDIA GPU evaluation driver ├── src/ │ ├── hrm_agent/ # Core agent logic, CLI, server, code-actions, and state machine │ ├── judge/ # SandboxRunner (wait4), TerminalBench, and fuzz oracle │ └── training/ # DatasetMiner, LoRA SFT/DPO trainers, and latent reasoner trainer └── tests/ # Comprehensive test suite (44/44 tests passing) ``` --- ## Installation & Quickstart ### Prerequisites - Python 3.10+ (Python 3.12 recommended) - `uv` (recommended) or standard `pip` - NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12+ (optional for GPU training/acceleration; CPU fallback supported) ### Setup ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/seeramsujay/hrmagent.git cd hrmagent # Create virtual environment and install in editable mode uv venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e . ``` --- ## Usage ### 1. Run TerminalBench Execute the standardized 5-task agentic terminal benchmark: ```bash hrm terminalbench ``` *Output: 100.0% Pass Rate (5/5 tasks passed in 287 ms).* ### 2. Solve a Problem with the Four-Model Agent Solve a competitive programming challenge using the 4-tier pipeline: ```bash hrm 4m-solve --problem-file examples/codechef_problem_example.json --language python ``` ### 3. Launch Localhost Server (OpenAI Compatible) Launch the REST server exposing both HRM endpoints and standard OpenAI endpoints: ```bash hrm serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --mode mock ``` Interactive Swagger documentation is available at: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`. ### 4. Head-to-Head Benchmark Evaluation Run the comparative benchmark of Baseline Sub-1B vs HRM-4M across 10 CodeChef/Codeforces problems: ```bash python src/judge/compare_4m_vs_baseline.py ``` ### 5. Train the HRM Latent Reasoner Fine-tune the latent continuous recurrence weights on CodeChef and high-star open source invariants: ```bash hrm 4m-train-latent --output-dir outputs/checkpoints_hrm_latent --epochs 5 ``` --- ## Benchmark Results ### TerminalBench (5 Tasks) | Task ID | Category | Verdict | Latency (ms) | Operational Task | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **TB-01-LOG-METRICS** | `log_diagnostics` | **PASS** | 13.9 | Parse access logs, compute HTTP status code distribution, isolate failure endpoint. | | **TB-02-BINARY-SEARCH-PATCH** | `code_patching` | **PASS** | 11.8 | Diagnose `IndexError` on empty arrays; patch boundary logic and verify 6 edge cases. | | **TB-03-CPP-INT64-OVERFLOW** | `build_compilation` | **PASS** | 235.9 | Fix 32-bit int overflow on $N=10^9$ with `int64_t`; compile C++20 with `-O3`. | | **TB-04-RECURSIVE-YAML-REFACTOR** | `bash_scripting` | **PASS** | 4.3 | Execute multi-file recursive `sed` refactoring over `configs/`. | | **TB-05-UNITTEST-DIAGNOSTIC-REPAIR** | `test_repair` | **PASS** | 30.6 | Diagnose `ZeroDivisionError` in analytics; patch code and pass 3/3 unit tests. | **Total Wall Time**: **287.1 ms** | **Pass Rate**: **100.0%** ### Competitive Programming: Baseline 0.5B vs HRM-4M | Benchmark Suite | Total Problems | Baseline 0.5B AC | HRM-4M AC | Baseline Pass % | HRM-4M Pass % | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **CodeChef & Codeforces CP** | 10 | 1 / 10 | **10 / 10** | 10.0% | **100.0%** | Full comparative details are documented in [`docs/BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md`](docs/BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md). --- ## Documentation Links - [Architecture & Latent Recurrence Specification](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - [API & CLI Reference Manual](docs/API_REFERENCE.md) - [Benchmarking & Evaluation Guide](docs/BENCHMARK_GUIDE.md) - [Academic Research Preprint (HRM-4M)](docs/HRM_FOUR_MODEL_PAPER.md) - [Comprehensive Hardware Evaluation Report](reports/benchmark_report.md) --- ## Testing & Linting Run full verification: ```bash # Run 44 automated tests pytest tests/ -v # Run linters black --check src tests ruff format --check src tests ruff check src tests flake8 src tests ``` --- ## License Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

readme:
microintegrated-flet

Build realtime web, mobile and desktop apps in Python only. No frontend experience required.

---

Build cross-platform apps in Python. No frontend experience required.

Flet is a Python framework for building web, desktop, and mobile apps without prior experience in frontend development. > **[Try Flet online in Flet Studio](https://studio.flet.dev)** > > Create, run, and share Python apps in your browser. Start from an example, write your own code, or get help from the AI agent. No installation required. ###    One Python codebase, six platforms Build your interface and application logic in Python, and run your app on iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, and web. No Dart, Swift, Kotlin, HTML, or JavaScript required. ###    150+ built-in controls and services Create your interface with ready-made layouts, buttons, forms, navigation, and dialogs. Customize colors, typography, and themes, with Material and Cupertino controls to suit your app. ###    Declarative UI for growing apps Organize your app into reusable components and let the UI update when application state changes. Prefer changing controls directly? The imperative style is supported too. [Compare the approaches](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/declarative-vs-imperative). ###    Your Python libraries, on mobile Use libraries such as NumPy, pandas, Pillow, and cryptography in your mobile apps. Flet provides [prebuilt binary packages](https://pypi.flet.dev) for iOS and Android, so you don't have to compile native dependencies yourself. ###    Run in the browser or on your server Run Python directly in the browser with Pyodide and WebAssembly, with no Python server required. Or keep your Python code on a server and deliver real-time UI updates to the browser. ###    Built-in packaging Use `flet build` to package your app for desktop, mobile, or web distribution, including the App Store and Google Play. Configure dependencies, icons, and platform settings in your project's `pyproject.toml`. ### ⚡   μFlet: Microcontroller & Hardware Suite Connect, stream telemetry, and flash firmware to microcontrollers directly from Python. With [`uflet`](https://flet.dev/docs/uflet), integrate ESP32 and RP2040 boards into your apps with async serial streaming, UF2/esptool flash engines, and pre-built widgets (`DeviceSelector`, `SerialConsole`, `FlashProgress`). Supports Desktop, WebSerial in browser, and Android USB-OTG. ###    Test your app on desktop and mobile Write [integration tests with pytest](https://flet.dev/docs/getting-started/integration-testing) and run them against your packaged app with `flet test`. Tap buttons, enter text, and verify user flows on desktop and mobile, with screenshot comparisons on Android and iOS. ###    Build with help from AI Explore and create apps with the AI agent in [Flet Studio](https://studio.flet.dev), or connect your coding assistant to the [Flet MCP server](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/flet-mcp) for version-specific API information and tools to find examples and icons. ###    Extensible Build custom controls in Python by composing existing controls, or create extensions that wrap Flutter packages to add new UI components and platform integrations. ###    Accessible Add screen-reader labels, tooltips, keyboard shortcuts, and custom semantics to help more people use your app. Inspect the accessibility information your UI exposes with the [semantics debugger](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/accessibility#debugging-semantics). ## Flet app example This simple counter app displays a number in the center of the screen. Press the **+** button to increment it: ```python import flet as ft def main(page: ft.Page): counter = ft.Text("0", size=50, data=0) def increment_click(e): counter.data += 1 counter.value = str(counter.data) page.floating_action_button = ft.FloatingActionButton( icon=ft.Icons.ADD, on_click=increment_click ) page.add( ft.SafeArea( expand=True, content=ft.Container( content=counter, alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER, ), ) ) ft.run(main) ``` To run the app, install `flet`: ```bash pip install 'flet[all]' ``` Save the code as `counter.py`, then launch the app: ```bash flet run counter.py ``` This opens the app in a native desktop window. The screenshot below shows it after pressing **+** three times:

To run the same app in your browser, add `--web`: ```bash flet run --web counter.py ```

name: Netra-UGV
description: High-performance, vision-based autonomous navigation stack for outdoor UGVs, engineered for GPS-denied environments and unstructured terrain.
readme:
Netra-UGV

Autonomous mobile robotics & UGV navigation stack with sim tests

--- # 🤖 NETRA-UGV: Vision-Based Autonomous Navigation for Outdoor Unmanned Ground Vehicles [![Smart India Hackathon 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/SIH_2026-PS--26126-orange.svg)](https://www.sih.gov.in/) [![Organization](https://img.shields.io/badge/Organization-Bharat_Electronics_Limited_(BEL)-blue.svg)](https://bel-india.in/) [![ROS 2 Humble](https://img.shields.io/badge/ROS_2-Humble-3498db.svg)](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/) [![Edge AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Edge_AI-BiSeNetV2_INT8-2ecc71.svg)](https://developer.nvidia.com/tensorrt) [![Visual SLAM](https://img.shields.io/badge/Localization-500Hz_MSCKF_OpenVINS-f39c12.svg)](./docs/MASTER_PROJECT_REPORT.md) [![Planning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Planner-Kinodynamic_TEB_+_v--Disparity-9b59b6.svg)](./docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) [![Live GCS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live_GCS-netraugv.vercel.app-blueviolet.svg)](https://netraugv.vercel.app) > **High-performance, vision-based autonomous navigation stack engineered for unstructured outdoor environments under complete GPS outage, dynamic lighting conditions, and negative obstacle hazards.** > > **Team:** KernelCrew (Team ID: 158370) > **Problem Statement ID:** SIH26126 — *Vision Based Autonomous Navigation for Unmanned Ground Vehicle for Outdoor environment* > **Theme:** Smart Automation | **Category:** Software | **Organization:** Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) --- ## 🎯 Executive Summary & Mission Profile Outdoor Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) operating in real-world environments face unpredictable terrain, variable lighting, dense foliage, and unreliable or blocked GPS signals. **NETRA-UGV** provides an end-to-end vision-centric autonomous navigation stack that enables cost-effective, data-rich outdoor traversal without dependency on expensive LiDAR or fragile satellite signals. Targeted at BEL's outdoor robotics platforms, NETRA-UGV addresses critical missions including: * 🚨 **Search-and-Rescue:** Navigating rubble, disaster zones, and collapsed infrastructure where GPS signals are heavily occluded. * 🌾 **Precision Agriculture:** Traversing uneven crop rows, mud, and tall grass while rejecting false stops from pliant vegetation. * 📦 **Remote Last-Mile Delivery:** Traversing unstructured rural tracks, forest trails, and GPS-deprived valleys safely from Point A to Point B. --- ## 🏆 Three Core Deliverables (PS-26126 Mapping) | Challenge / Deliverable | NETRA-UGV Technical Solution | Benchmark & Verification | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Path Detection (Perception AI)** | Lightweight **BiSeNetV2-Lite** bilateral segmentation network trained on off-road **RELLIS-3D** dataset. Classifies terrain into solid ground, pliant vegetation, mud hazard, and rigid barriers. | **76.25% mIoU** on RELLIS-3D off-road validation; **2.6 ms** inference latency via INT8 TensorRT on Jetson Orin Nano. | | **2. Visual Localization (SLAM/Odometry)** | Stereo Visual-Inertial Odometry pipeline using **OpenVINS Multi-State Constraint Kalman Filter (MSCKF)** fused with high-frequency IMU and KLT optical feature tracking. | **< 1.2% translation drift** over 500 m GPS-denied closed loops; 50 Hz real-time update rate with zero external satellite dependence. | | **3. Collision Avoidance & Path Planning** | **Kinodynamic TEB (Timed Elastic Band) Local Planner** coupled with a geometric **$v$-Disparity negative obstacle raycaster** to identify ditches, trenches, and drop-offs. | Dynamic obstacle avoidance at up to **1.5 m/s**; detects >0.35 m ground drop-offs in **< 0.6 ms** with >2.3 s braking margin. | --- ## 🏗️ System Architecture & Block Diagram ``` [ Stereo Vision & 6-DOF IMU ] │ ├──► [ BiSeNetV2 Semantic Segmentation ] ──► Traversability Risk Matrix ──┐ │ │ ├──► [ OpenVINS MSCKF Odometry (50Hz) ] ──► 6-DOF Pose Estimation ───────┼──► [ 2.5D Rolling Costmap ] │ │ │ └──► [ v-Disparity Raycaster (<0.6ms) ] ──► Negative Obstacle Voids ─────┘ │ ▼ [ TEB Kinodynamic Planner ] │ ▼ [ Motor cmd_vel (PWM) ] ``` ![NETRA-UGV System Architecture](./docs/diagrams/Netra-UGV-block_diagram.png) 📄 **[Download High-Resolution System Architecture (PDF)](./docs/architecture_diagram.pdf)** --- ## ⚡ Quickstart Guide for Evaluators & Reviewers ### 1. 🎛️ Run the Web Ground Control Station (GCS Dashboard) * 🌐 **Production Deployment**: **[https://netraugv.vercel.app](https://netraugv.vercel.app)** The interactive GCS includes real-time telemetry, 2D waypoint mission planning, AI forward camera HUD with segmentation overlays, sensor view-switching, and multi-scenario autonomous simulation. ```bash # Navigate to the dashboard directory cd dashboard # Install dependencies (Node.js >= 18) pnpm install # Launch Vite development server pnpm dev ``` 👉 Open your browser at **[http://localhost:5173/](http://localhost:5173/)** to access the live dashboard. --- ### 2. 🧠 Run & Validate the BiSeNetV2 AI Perception Model Validate the off-road terrain segmentation ONNX model on authentic RELLIS-3D terrain samples. The dual-backend architecture automatically detects and leverages ONNX Runtime with GPU or falls back to OpenCV DNN. ```bash # Run standalone inference verification script python3 scripts/test_bisenetv2_onnx.py ``` * **Inputs:** `weights/bisenetv2_rellis.onnx` & `weights/sample_terrain.jpg` ($1024 \times 448$ RGB) * **Outputs Generated:** * Segmentation Mask: [`weights/test_segmentation_mask.png`](./weights/test_segmentation_mask.png) * 50/50 Visual Overlay: [`weights/test_segmentation_overlay.png`](./weights/test_segmentation_overlay.png) * **Terrain Classes:** `0: SOLID_GROUND`, `1: PLIANT_VEGETATION`, `2: MUD_HAZARD`, `3: RIGID_OBSTACLE` --- ### 3. 🛰️ Multi-Engine Simulation Subsystems (Webots & Gazebo) #### A. Webots Autonomous Outdoor Mission Simulation Run the standalone simulation engine modeling 4 negative obstacle drop-offs, 28 boulders, and autonomous Point A → Point B traversal: ```bash # Run headless simulation & trajectory plot renderer python3 sim/webots/render.py # optional: --out DIR ``` * **Trajectory Output:** [`sim/webots/netra_ugv_sim_trajectory.png`](./sim/webots/netra_ugv_sim_trajectory.png) * **Interactive 3D Webots GUI:** Open Webots R2025a and load `sim/webots/worlds/netra_tactical.wbt` to visualize live collision avoidance and path tracking. #### B. Gazebo Outdoor Obstacle World & ROS 2 Bridge ```bash # In your ROS 2 Humble workspace: source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash colcon build --base-paths src sim source install/setup.bash # Launch full outdoor obstacle world and UGV skid-steer chassis ros2 launch netra_sim gazebo.launch.py ``` --- ## 📁 Repository Structure ``` Netra-UGV/ ├── dashboard/ # Web Ground Control Station (React 19, Vite, TailwindCSS) │ ├── src/components/ # LiveView HUD, TacticalMapCanvas, TeleopJoystick, HealthPanel │ └── package.json # Scripts & dependencies ├── docs/ # Complete engineering blueprints & presentations │ ├── MASTER_PROJECT_REPORT.md # Comprehensive master engineering report │ ├── TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md # Deep-dive blueprint, POSIX scheduling & compute budget │ ├── PPT_SLIDES_DECK.md # Official presentation deck & presenter scripts │ ├── VIDEO_SCRIPT_5MIN.md # Timed 5-minute technical presentation script │ ├── WEIGHTS_AND_MODELS_GUIDE.md # Model weights & Jetson TensorRT compilation guide │ ├── WEIGHTS_AND_MODELS_TRAINING.md# RELLIS-3D training pipeline & benchmark results │ ├── WORK_COMPLETION_REPORT_TERRAIN_AI.md # End-to-end Terrain AI completion report │ ├── JURY_VIVA_QA_SHEET.md # High-yield jury viva Q&A defense sheet │ ├── SIM_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md # Simulation implementation blueprint │ ├── RESEARCH_FEEDER_BEL_UGV.md # Problem analysis, outdoor navigation & BOM spectrum │ └── architecture_diagram.pdf # High-resolution printable system architecture ├── scripts/ # Model testing, dataset verification & training scripts │ ├── test_bisenetv2_onnx.py # Universal ONNX/OpenCV inference test script │ ├── train_bisenetv2.py # PyTorch training pipeline on RELLIS-3D │ ├── export_bisenetv2_onnx.py # PyTorch to ONNX fixed-graph exporter │ └── verify_rellis_dataset.py # Dataset auditing & multi-sample visualization ├── sim/ # Multi-Engine Simulation Subsystems (Webots & Gazebo) │ ├── webots/ # Webots simulation (Pioneer 3-AT, ditches, rocks) │ │ ├── worlds/netra_tactical.wbt # 50x36m elevation grid with 4 ditches & 28 rocks │ │ ├── controllers/netra_ugv/ # Autonomous controller with waypoint navigation │ │ ├── render.py # Headless 20 Hz simulation & trajectory plot generator │ │ └── gen_world.py # Procedural terrain & obstacle world generator │ ├── config/gz_bridge.yaml # Gazebo-to-ROS 2 parameter bridge mapping │ ├── launch/full_demo.launch.py # Master Gazebo simulation launch file │ ├── models/ugv_skidsteer/ # Skid-steer UGV URDF with stereo camera & IMU │ └── worlds/tactical_obstacle.world# Negative obstacle ditch & outdoor terrain world ├── src/ # ROS 2 Humble Autonomous Packages │ ├── netra_msgs/ # Custom message definitions (Terrain, Costmap, Failsafe) │ ├── netra_perception/ # BiSeNetV2 inference + Ground-ROI crop + Lens obscuration detection │ ├── netra_localization/ # OpenVINS MSCKF + KLT tracker + 500 Hz IMU fusion │ ├── netra_mapping/ # 2.5D risk costmap + v-Disparity negative obstacle raycaster │ ├── netra_planning/ # Kinodynamic TEB local planner + tip-over safety guards │ └── netra_security/ # Robust CAN-FD driver & secure node communication policies └── weights/ # Model weights, calibration tools & artifacts ├── bisenetv2_rellis.onnx # Optimized ONNX model (8.79 MB) ├── bisenetv2_rellis_best.pth # Trained PyTorch checkpoint (76.25% mIoU) ├── bisenetv2_rellis_int8.trt # INT8 TensorRT engine stub └── scripts/ # TensorRT INT8 calibrator & trtexec compilation scripts ``` --- ## 🤖 Core Subsystems Breakdown ### 1. Edge AI Perception (`netra_perception`) * **Model:** BiSeNetV2-Lite (2.31M parameters) trained on RELLIS-3D outdoor benchmark. * **Input Resolution:** $1024 \times 448 \times 3$ with dynamic Ground-Horizon ROI crop removing sky and vehicle hood vibration. * **Inference Rate:** $15\text{ Hz}$ on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano ($2.6\text{ ms}$ latency via INT8 TensorRT). * **Lens Clearing:** Dynamic lens obscuration detection triggers automated lens clearing sequence in dusty or muddy conditions. ### 2. GPS-Denied Visual Localization (`netra_localization`) * **Core:** Multi-State Constraint Kalman Filter (MSCKF) based on OpenVINS. * **Fusion Rate:** 500 Hz IMU pre-integration tightly coupled with 30 Hz stereo optical flow feature tracks. * **Anti-Drift:** Zero-Velocity Updates (ZUPT) and kinodynamic skid-steer slip compensation, bounding drift to $< 1.2\%$ over 500 m. ### 3. Negative Obstacle Costmapping & Planning (`netra_mapping` & `netra_planning`) * **$v$-Disparity Ditch Raycaster:** Analyzes geometric disparity gradients to identify ditches, trenches, and drop-offs ($> 0.35\text{ m}$ depth) undetectable by single-line planar LiDARs. * **Kinodynamic TEB Planner:** Timed-Elastic-Band local trajectory optimization respecting dynamic tilt limits ($\theta_{\text{roll}} \le 22^\circ$) and governing speeds through mud ($0.4\text{ m/s}$) and pliant vegetation ($0.5\text{ m/s}$). ### 4. Rugged Edge Compute & Thermal Envelope * **Edge Hardware:** NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (40 TOPS) or Raspberry Pi 5 + Hailo-8 NPU (26 TOPS). * **Power Efficiency:** Sub-13.5W compute power budget enabling 14+ hours continuous operation on a standard 200Wh battery pack. * **Ruggedization:** IP67 weather-sealed fanless enclosure rated for $-10^\circ\text{C}$ to $+55^\circ\text{C}$ outdoor operating conditions. --- ## name: oxygenated-routine
description: A privacy-first, GenAI-powered assistant providing real-time, actionable urban air quality guidance to help families manage winter smog effectively.
readme: # Oxygenated Routine A GenAI-powered assistant that helps families and communities get through severe winter smog. Type your city (or tap **Use my location**) and it checks the live air quality, then tells you in plain language: - **what to do today**: three clear actions first, then a full low-emission daily routine, - **when to go out**: the cleanest hours in the next 24 hours, - **how to clean the air at home**: indoor air hacks that fit your budget, - **which greener swaps help**: commute, heating and cooking changes that cut emissions too, - **what each choice changes**: for example, "roughly like smoking 3.8 cigarettes today, 1.3 with this plan". ## Chosen vertical **Urban air-pollution and winter-smog assistant for families and communities.** The persona is a busy parent, or a neighbourhood group, in a smog-hit city who wants to know _what do I actually do today, and does it make a difference?_ without reading AQI charts. ## Using it 1. Open the app and type your city, tap **Use my location**, or tap an example city (Delhi, Lahore, Beijing). 2. Press **Get my plan**. That is the whole flow: one step, no sign-up. 3. Optionally open **Personalise my plan** (household, health conditions, commute, heating, cooking, budget, your own notes) and press **Update my plan** at the bottom. The advice then fits your home. Without it, a typical household is assumed, and the summary says so with a one-tap **Make it fit my home** link. The results page opens with the answer and is built to be read in seconds: - the AQI as a number, a plain-language meaning and a colour scale showing where today sits between clean and hazardous, - **Do these 3 things first**, - bars comparing today's exposure on current habits with the plan, - the cleanest time to go out and a low-emission day plan, - longer reference sections (indoor air hacks, greener swaps, community actions) folded behind a tap, each with a teaser such as "4 ideas, 3 free". The jump menu opens them. Safety sections (looking after vulnerable people, when to get medical help) are never folded. ## Approach and logic The design rule is **the model explains; code decides the numbers.** ```text browser ──► POST /api/plan ──► validate (zod) ──► resolve place + live AQI (Open-Meteo) │ deterministic engines ◄──────────┘ • AQI category + outdoor guidance (stricter for sensitive households) • cleanest 2-hour window from the hourly forecast • impact engine (exposure, CO₂e) from documented factors │ verified facts ──┴──► Claude (structured output, schema-checked) │ └─ on error / refusal / bad output ─┐ ▼ ▼ plan JSON ◄────────────── offline rule engine (same schema) ``` - **Logical decisions from context.** The same AQI is judged more cautiously when the household has children, seniors or a heart or lung condition. Advice changes with the air (good air does not alarm; hazardous air says stay in), with budget (a low budget never sees medium or high-cost hacks), with heating and cooking fuel (a wood fire gets a CO alarm and a cleaner-heating swap), and with commute (nobody is told to switch to something dirtier, and walking or cycling is only suggested for short trips). - **A time window is only suggested when it is clearly cleaner**: two consecutive waking hours in the next 24, at least 10 AQI points better than the worst waking hour, and labelled "tomorrow" when it is. If any hour of that window is still at an "avoid" level, the plan only suggests essential trips with a respirator, never outdoor play. On an "avoid" day, even a safe window is for short essential trips only, so the plan never contradicts its own "keep play indoors" advice. - **Safety beats emissions.** On "avoid" days the plan never suggests walking or cycling, and the school-run swap becomes carpooling. Fireplace advice only closes the damper once the fire is out and the ashes are cold. These rules live in `src/safety.js` and apply to both paths: the rule engine follows them by construction, Claude is given them in its prompt (and is never handed walking or cycling options on avoid days), and every Claude plan is checked against them. The check reads every text field clause by clause, so "indoors" or "avoid" only counts for the clause it is in, and it recognises times written as 14:00 or 2 pm. A plan that breaks a rule is replaced by the rule engine's plan, with a notice. The check is deliberately strict, so an ambiguous sentence also triggers the fallback. - **Numbers come from code, not the model.** Every figure on the page (AQI, exposure, CO₂e, the time window) is computed in code and rendered from those values. Claude receives the same figures as `` and is told to quote only them. Its output is checked against the plan schema, which enforces structure (for example, medical red flags can never be empty) but cannot prove that every number in its sentences was copied correctly. That residual risk is why the headline figures are always rendered from code. - **Always useful.** With no API key, or if Claude errors or refuses, the rule engine returns the same plan shape and the UI says which one you got. ### How impact is estimated | Quantity | Method | | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Cigarette-equivalents | 22 µg/m³ of PM2.5 over 24 h ≈ 1 cigarette (Berkeley Earth rule of thumb) | | Indoor PM2.5 | ≈ 90% of outdoor with windows open, ≈ 60% closed, about half that with HEPA | | Respirator outdoors | A well-fitted N95/FFP2 cuts what you inhale by about 60% in everyday wear | | Commute CO₂e (kg per km) | car 0.17, motorbike 0.11, bus 0.10, metro 0.04, walking and cycling 0 | These are communication aids built from stated assumptions, not medical measurements. The app lists them under **How these numbers are estimated**. ## Running it Requires Node 22.22.2+, 24.15+ or 26+ (the versions the lint tooling supports). ```bash npm install npm start # http://127.0.0.1:3000, uses the built-in rule engine ``` To enable Claude-written plans: ```bash export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-key npm start ``` | Variable | Default | Purpose | | ------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | unset | Enables Claude; without it the rule engine runs | | `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `claude-opus-5-5` | Model used for plans | | `DISABLE_LLM` | unset | Set to `1` to force the rule engine | | `PORT`, `HOST` | `3000`, `127.0.0.1` | Where the server listens | | `TRUST_PROXY` | unset | Set to `1` only behind a proxy that appends the client address to `X-Forwarded-For` | ## Project layout ```text src/ server.js HTTP server, routing, security headers, static files planner.js orchestrates one request airData.js Open-Meteo geocoding + air quality, cleanest-window search aqi.js AQI categories (with plain-language meanings), PM2.5 conversion impact.js deterministic exposure and CO₂e engine rules.js offline plan builder (same schema as Claude) safety.js safety rules shared by both paths, and the check every Claude plan must pass llm.js Claude call: prompt, structured output, refusal handling profile.js request validation and defaults planSchema.js plan shape shared by Claude and the rule engine rateLimit.js fixed-window limiter public/ accessible, framework-free front end (ES modules) test/ node:test suite ``` ## Security - API key stays server-side; the browser never sees it. - All input is validated with Zod (types, ranges, enums, length limits) and control characters are stripped. - User free text is passed to Claude in a separate `` block, treated as data, with angle brackets neutralised so it cannot close its own tag. The model's output is schema-validated before use. - Strict Content-Security-Policy (no inline scripts or styles), `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, frame blocking and a narrow Permissions-Policy. - Server text is inserted into the page only via `textContent`, never as HTML. - Body-size limit (16 KB), JSON-only content type, per-client rate limits (plan requests are limited most tightly because they can call a paid API), and path-traversal-safe static serving. - Errors returned to clients are generic; logs never contain profiles or model output. - Nothing is stored on the server. Answers are remembered only in the user's own browser (`localStorage`) and can be cleared from the footer. Browser location is rounded to about 1 km before it is sent. ## Accessibility Semantic landmarks and a skip link; collapsible sections use the WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern (a button inside a real heading, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`); the AQI scale and impact bars are decorative (`aria-hidden`) because the same facts are given in text; busy buttons say what is happening and the form is marked `aria-busy`; every control has a visible label and hint; fieldsets and legends group questions; live regions announce progress and errors; focus moves to the results heading; air quality is conveyed by text and number, never colour alone; 44 px touch targets; visible focus rings; light and dark themes; reduced-motion support; layouts work from small phones upwards; the forecast is a real table with a caption and column headers. ## Testing ```bash npm test # 184 tests, offline, no API key needed npm run lint # ESLint, Stylelint, HTMLHint, Prettier, cspell ``` The suite uses Node's built-in runner, a fake Open-Meteo and a fake Claude client, and jsdom for the UI. It covers AQI banding, the impact maths, validation and sanitising, upstream failures, the rule engine across AQI levels and household types, Claude request shape and prompt-injection handling, fallbacks on error, refusal and invalid output, every HTTP security behaviour (headers, 400, 404, 405, 413, 415, 429, traversal), safe rendering, collapsible sections and the jump menu, and AQI scale positioning. ## Assumptions and limits - AQI and PM2.5 come from Open-Meteo's global model, so values near a city can differ from a local monitor. A manual AQI field lets people enter their own reading, which also makes the app work offline. - The US EPA AQI scale is used everywhere. - When the user doesn't personalise, a typical household is assumed: two adults, no children, an 8 km car commute five days a week, electric heating, gas cooking and a medium budget. - Impact figures are rule-of-thumb estimates; guidance is general wellbeing information, not medical advice. Red-flag symptoms and "get medical help" guidance are always shown. - Behind a proxy (`TRUST_PROXY=1`) the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry is used, because left-hand entries can be forged by the client. Only enable it when the proxy **appends** the connecting client's address to `X-Forwarded-For`. A proxy that passes a client-supplied header through unchanged would let clients choose their own rate-limit key. - A manual AQI is used once and never remembered, so a later visit always checks the live air. - Rate limiting is in-memory and per process; run behind a shared limiter if you scale to several instances. - The Claude path is exercised in tests with a fake client. Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to use it for real.

name: remote-zed
description: Secure, end-to-end encrypted remote workspace client for Zed, enabling full mobile control of AI agents and Git workflows via firewall-proof tunnels.
readme:
remote-zed

End-to-end Encrypted Zed Remote Workspace Client (Flutter + Rust + Python)

---
# ⚡ Zed Remote **Control your local Zed AI sessions, approve agent tool permissions, execute Git workflows, and command host workspaces directly from your mobile phone.** [![CI](https://github.com/seeramsujay/remote-zed/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/seeramsujay/remote-zed/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Android](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Android_12+-3DDC84?logo=android&logoColor=white)](https://android.com) [![Jetpack Compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/UI-Jetpack_Compose_Material_3-4285F4?logo=jetpackcompose&logoColor=white)](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/compose) [![Rust Daemon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Daemon-Rust_Tokio-dea584?logo=rust&logoColor=white)](https://rust-lang.org) [![Zed Compatible](https://img.shields.io/badge/Editor-Zed_Official-087EA4?logo=rust&logoColor=white)](https://zed.dev) [![Tunnel Security](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tunnel-AES--256--GCM_%2B_SSH_443-purple?logo=wireguard&logoColor=white)](#bunker-tunnel-firewall-bypass)
```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeramsujay/remote-zed/main/install.sh | bash ``` [Features](#key-features) • [Quick Start](#quick-start) • [Mobile Apps](#mobile-app-setup) • [Bunker Tunnel](#bunker-tunnel-firewall-bypass) • [Desktop Integration](#zero-rebuild-integration-with-official-zed) • [Architecture](#architecture) • [Releases](#releases-cloud-builds)
--- ## 💡 Why Zed Remote? When working away from your desk—whether commuting, in a college hostel, or traveling—your primary machine stays running at your workstation. Modern development workflows rely on autonomous AI agents (like AntiGravity, Claude, or custom ACP agents) to refactor code, run tests, and execute bash commands. **Traditional remote tools fail on mobile:** - **VNC / RDP / Graphical Desktops**: Consume massive bandwidth, suffer high latency, and scale horribly to 6-inch phone screens. - **Tailscale / WireGuard**: Frequently blocked on restrictive networks (e.g. Fortinet, college Wi-Fi, or corporate firewalls blocking UDP 41641). **Zed Remote solves this at the protocol level:** Instead of streaming pixels, Zed Remote intercepts the **Agent Client Protocol (ACP)** JSON-RPC streams over standard I/O pipes. It forwards token-by-token reasoning chunks, tool approval cards, and repository state directly to the native **Android (Material 3 / Jetpack Compose)** app (with native iOS Swift client planned for v0.2.0) over a firewall-proof, AES-256-GCM encrypted tunnel. --- ## ✨ Key Features | Feature | Description | | :--- | :--- | | 💬 **Real-Time ACP AI Stream** | Monitor streaming reasoning chunks, thoughts, and conversational turns with your desktop AI agent from anywhere. | | 🛡️ **Remote Tool Authorization** | Receive instant prompts on your phone to approve or deny file edits, deletions, or terminal commands triggered by the agent. | | 💻 **Termux-Style Shell** | Interactive mobile terminal equipped with a virtual quick-keys bar (`TAB`, `~`, `/`, `-`, `|`, `..`, `↑`, `↓`, `Ctrl+C`, `CLEAR`) for quick CLI tasks. | | 📁 **Workspace Control & Folder Opening** | Browse remote directories, create new project folders, and tap **"Set Workspace"** to instantly open that project inside the desktop Zed GUI via local socket IPC. | | 🌿 **Mobile Git Operations** | Review diffs with syntax highlighting, stage modified files, write commit messages, and push to GitHub/GitLab directly from your phone. | | 🎨 **Material 3 / Material You** | Handcrafted native Jetpack Compose interface with Android 12+ wallpaper dynamic color extraction and obsidian dark mode. | | 🏰 **Bunker Tunnel (Zero-Trust)** | Outbound reverse tunnel over SSH port 443 that bypasses Fortinet firewalls with zero-knowledge, 48-char random hex rendezvous and end-to-end AES-256-GCM encryption. | --- ## 🏗️ Architecture Zed Remote places a lightweight proxy daemon between Zed and your AI agent executable, with an encrypted rendezvous for mobile devices: ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Desktop Workstation │ │ │ │ ┌──────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ │ │ │ Zed Editor │◄── Stdio IPC ──►│ AntiGravity │ │ │ └──────▲───────┘ (NDJSON-RPC) │ (AI Agent) │ │ │ │ └───────▲───────┘ │ │ └───────────────┬─────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ ┌────────────▼────────────┐ │ │ │ zed-remote-daemon │ │ │ │ • Dual HTTP & WS Engine│ │ │ │ • ACP Stream Router │ │ │ │ • Git & Shell Executor │ │ │ └────────────┬────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ ┌────────────▼────────────┐ │ │ │ Bunker Tunnel Script │ │ │ │ (SSH 443 + AES-256-GCM)│ │ │ └────────────┬────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┘ │ Outbound TCP 443 (Firewall Proof) ▼ Pinggy Relay + ntfy Encrypted Rendezvous ▲ │ Decrypts with Scanned Key ┌────────────┴────────────┐ │ Mobile Client │ │ • Android Jetpack M3 │ │ • (iOS Swift in v0.2.0) │ └─────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ## 🚀 Quick Start ### ⚡ Complete One-Line Install (Laptop) Run this single command on your laptop to install Zed Remote, configure Zed, and set up your bunker tunnel (interactive prompt allows enabling an automatic systemd background service): ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeramsujay/remote-zed/main/install.sh | bash ``` #### 1. Bind your phone once: ```bash zed-tunnel --bind ``` Scan the terminal QR code once in the mobile app. The session channel and AES-GCM encryption key are permanently saved on both devices. #### 2. Everyday connection (no QR scanning needed): ```bash zed-tunnel ``` Starts the tunnel and dynamically publishes encrypted updates to your phone in the background. #### 3. Autostart & Service Management: ```bash zed-tunnel --service enable # Start automatically on system boot via systemd user service zed-tunnel --service disable # Revert to on-demand mode zed-tunnel --inject # Re-inject daemon into Zed settings.json zed-tunnel --status # Check tunnel and systemd service status zed-tunnel -h # Display help and commands zed-tunnel --update # Update Zed Remote to latest release # Note: You can use "zedt" as a shorthand for "zed-tunnel" anywhere! ``` --- ### 📱 Mobile App Setup - 🤖 **Native Jetpack Compose**: Download **`zed-remote.apk`** for Android 12+ dynamic Material You colors, rapid UI rendering, full ACP AI streaming, mobile Git panel, and integrated terminal. *(Note: iOS Swift client is scheduled for v0.2.0; Flutter builds are paused).* 1. **Install App**: Download `zed-remote.apk` from [**Releases**](https://github.com/seeramsujay/remote-zed/releases). 2. **Scan QR Code**: Open the app, tap the **Scan QR** icon, and scan the terminal QR code printed by `zed-tunnel`. 3. **Control From Anywhere**: Prompt your agent, approve tool actions, run terminal commands, and open project folders off-the-grid! --- ## 🏰 Bunker Tunnel & Firewall Bypass Standard mesh overlays like Tailscale or WireGuard use UDP (port 41641), which enterprise networks, university hostels, and Fortinet egress firewalls routinely block or throttle via Deep Packet Inspection (DPI). **How the Bunker Tunnel works:** 1. **Outbound Port 443 Only**: Establishes an outbound reverse SSH tunnel over port 443 (indistinguishable from standard HTTPS traffic). 2. **Ephemeral Rendezvous**: Generates a cryptographically random topic (e.g. `zed-bunker-` + 48 hex characters) providing $10^{58}$ entropy, making collision or discovery impossible. 3. **AES-256-GCM Encryption**: The laptop encrypts the dynamic tunnel URL with a 256-bit symmetric key (`12-byte IV + ciphertext + 16-byte tag`) before posting to `ntfy.sh`. 4. **Zero Eavesdropping**: Third parties and relay servers see only random opaque ciphertext. The decryption key is scanned directly from your terminal and never transmitted over the network. --- ## 🧩 Zero-Rebuild Integration with Official Zed You never need to maintain a custom fork of Zed or compile Zed's 20GB+ Rust codebase on your laptop. Choose either integration option: ### Option 1: Daemon Injection (`inject-daemon.sh`) — *Recommended* Registers the proxy daemon in `~/.config/zed/settings.json`: - **Survives official updates**: When official Zed updates via `apt`, `.deb`, or auto-updater, your settings stay intact. - **Window Management**: Opening folders or setting workspaces on mobile automatically executes `zed ` over `~/.local/share/zed/zed-stable.sock` to open that folder in the desktop GUI. ```bash ./tools/inject-daemon.sh ``` ### Option 2: Native Zed Dev Extension (`install-extension.sh`) Symlinks the extension at `extensions/zed-remote` into Zed's dev extension path: - Registers `zed-remote` as an MCP context server. - Adds `/bunker status` and `/bunker pair` slash commands directly inside Zed's Agent panel. ```bash ./tools/install-extension.sh ``` --- ## 📦 Releases & Cloud Builds You don't need to heat up your laptop compiling binaries. GitHub Actions automatically builds and publishes releases on GitHub's cloud runners for free: ```bash # Tag and push to trigger automated cloud build git tag v0.1.2 git push origin v0.1.2 ``` GitHub Actions compiles in parallel and attaches the following release assets: - 🤖 **`zed-remote.apk`**: Native Material 3 / Jetpack Compose Android client. - 🐧 **`zed-remote-daemon-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`**: Precompiled high-performance Rust host daemon binary. - 🏰 **`bunker-tunnel.sh`**: Fortinet-proof SSH 443 + AES-256-GCM tunnel & QR generator. - 💉 **`inject-daemon.sh`**: Zero-rebuild official Zed configuration injector. *(Note: iOS Swift client is scheduled for v0.2.0; Flutter builds are paused).* To build manually on your workstation: ```bash # Build Compose APK ./build-all.sh compose # Build Rust daemon ./build-all.sh daemon ``` --- ## 📂 Repository Structure ``` remote-zed/ ├── android/ # Native Android App (Material 3, Jetpack Compose, dynamic colors) │ ├── app/src/main/ # UI Screens, ViewModel, Terminal, Files, and Bunker client │ └── build.gradle.kts ├── app/ # Cross-platform Flutter App (Android & iOS) │ ├── lib/ # Dual-panel layout, ACP streaming, Terminal, Bunker crypto │ └── pubspec.yaml ├── daemon/ # High-performance Rust host daemon (Tokio, ACP Proxy, Git & Shell engine) │ ├── src/gateway/ # Dual HTTP REST/SSE and WebSocket gateway │ ├── src/terminal/ # Terminal execution and remote filesystem operations │ └── Cargo.toml ├── extensions/ # Native Zed Dev Extension │ └── zed-remote/ # extension.toml, MCP context server, /bunker slash command ├── tools/ # One-shot automation scripts │ ├── bunker-tunnel.sh# Fortinet-proof SSH 443 + AES-256-GCM tunnel & QR generator │ ├── inject-daemon.sh# Automatic official Zed settings.json injector │ └── install-extension.sh # Symlinks dev extension into Zed ├── install.sh # One-line automated host installer ├── patches/ # Reference GPUI gateway patches for Zed desktop ├── build-all.sh # Local one-shot compilation script └── .github/workflows/ # Automated CI and release build pipelines ```
